clue.text: Expert East European leader writer

parts.note: a Pole is an East European, and the adjective is Polish
ED, short for editor, the person who writes a newspaper's leaders (editorials)

explanation.surface: A specialist from Eastern Europe who writes newspaper editorials.
explanation.walkthrough: A newspaper's 'leader' is its editorial column, written by the editor, abbreviated ED.
explanation.definitionFit: A polished performer is a refined, accomplished one, so the adjective can stand for expert.

clue.text: Promise a brief conversation

definitions.meaning: to give your ... is to promise
to have a ... with someone is to speak briefly

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses are idioms: giving one's word is a pledge, and 'a word' is a short chat.

clue.text: Matter brought up gets overlooked by a theologian's tots

indicators.note: in a down entry the piece below is overlooked by the pieces placed above it

parts.note: DD is a Doctor of Divinity, a theologian

indicators.note: in a down clue the word for matter is read upward, so backwards

parts.note: pus is the matter in an infected wound

explanation.surface: Something mentioned is ignored by a theologian's small children.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tots' looks like children but is the verb, as in totting up a bill.
explanation.definitionFit: To tot is to add figures together, the same idiom as totting up a total.

clue.text: With German uniform colour Spooner's managing to desexualise the wife

indicators.note: the Reverend Spooner swapped the opening sounds of words, so two words here trade first letters

parts.note: to geld an animal is to castrate it
Frau is German for wife, chiming with the German theme

explanation.surface: Spooner, dressed in German uniform colour, is trying to neuter his spouse.
explanation.walkthrough: GELD FRAU with first letters swapped gives FELD GRAU.
explanation.definitionFit: Feldgrau, field grey, was the colour of the German army's uniforms in both world wars.

clue.text: London associate in days gone by played him and Cole

definitions.text: London associate in days gone by

indicators.note: the letters are played with, jumbled into a new order

explanation.surface: A musician performed works by two composers, including Cole Porter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'me old china' is Cockney rhyming slang: china plate = mate, a London friend, now rather dated.
explanation.definitionFit: The cockney phrase means 'my mate', a friend or associate, in old-time London speech.

clue.text: See 11
See 25
Shade of difference one noticed in sister establishment

indicators.note: the letter is spotted inside the word for the sister

parts.note: a nun is a religious sister
A means one
CE, the Church of England, often called the Establishment

explanation.surface: A subtle distinction spotted in a convent where sisters live.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sister establishment' reads as a convent, but it splits in two: 'the Establishment' is a nickname for Britain's state church.
explanation.definitionFit: A nuance is a slight variation in meaning or tone, a fine distinction.

clue.text: Man or woman's name's brought up regularly

indicators.note: the letter for name is moved up to an earlier place in the word

parts.note: Evelyn is a name given to both men and women, such as Evelyn Waugh
N is the abbreviation for name

explanation.surface: A unisex name is mentioned at regular intervals.
explanation.walkthrough: EVELYN has its N moved forward to give EVENLY.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something evenly means at a steady, uniform rate, as regularly does.

clue.text: Advice given when 17? Watch this space!

definitions.meaning: the warning broadcast to passengers when travelling on the Tube, 17 being the answer for using the Underground
read literally, watch is ... and this space is the gap

explanation.definitionFit: The London Underground warning to step carefully over the platform gap is also a literal instruction to watch a space.

clue.text: Advice given when 17? Odd fact: personal stereos heal suffering!

indicators.note: these words are in a bad way, so their letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A peculiar claim that headphones cure ailments.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Odd' looks like the anagram signal but is part of the fodder; 'suffering' does the jumbling. 17 is TUBING, travelling on the Tube.
explanation.definitionFit: The recorded warning on London Underground trains as doors close is advice for passengers.

clue.text: See 10
Welcome news is nothing, filling snack up with some corn

indicators.note: the zero goes inside the reversed snack
in a down clue the word for the snack is read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: a hot dog is a snack
O looks like zero, nothing
an ear is a head of corn

explanation.surface: Good news means having nothing but a sandwich and some corn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' reverses HOTDOG to GODTOH; 'filling' puts O inside it after GO.
explanation.definitionFit: Something good to hear is news that is welcome to the listener.

clue.text: Craft of stretching hides and initially consulting sources of great wisdom

indicators.note: only the opening letter of the word consulting is taken

parts.note: oracles were consulted for prophetic wisdom

explanation.surface: Tanning skins and asking wise people for guidance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Craft' reads as a skill, but it is a boat: the coracle is built of hide stretched over a wicker frame.
explanation.definitionFit: A coracle is a small round boat traditionally made by stretching animal hide over a frame.

clue.text: Accumulation of what's wet and dry, providing vehicle for theatre performances?

indicators.note: the outer word carries the other inside it

parts.note: the word is used as written
operations, OPS, are what surgeons perform in an operating theatre

explanation.surface: Rain and drought both, as staging for plays.
explanation.walkthrough: 'theatre' suggests the stage, but it is an operating theatre.
explanation.definitionFit: Dropsy is the old medical term for oedema, a build-up of watery fluid in the body.

clue.text: Like reticent one quaffing rum made so poorly?

indicators.note: drinking in, so the word for rum goes inside

parts.note: shily, a spelling of shyly, means in the way of a reticent person
rum means strange, odd

explanation.surface: Someone shy downing rum and making a bad job of it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rum' looks like the drink, but it is the British adjective meaning strange.
explanation.definitionFit: Shoddily means in a careless, badly made way, which is to say poorly.

clue.text: A tower of strength accepting container for pipes

indicators.note: the boat takes the container inside it

parts.note: a tug is a powerful boat that tows
a bin is a container

explanation.surface: A dependable person holding a vessel for pipes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A tower of strength' is a reliable person, but read literally it is a strong boat that tows. Elsewhere in the puzzle TUBING also means riding the Tube.
explanation.definitionFit: Tubing is a length of tubes, so it serves as a collective word for pipes.

clue.text: Starve two beasts going over lines

indicators.note: in a down clue the beasts are turned over, read upward

parts.note: a gnu is an African antelope
a hog is a pig
RY is the abbreviation for railway, the lines

explanation.surface: Two animals cross railway tracks with nothing to eat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going over' reverses GNU + HOG, giving GOHUNG.
explanation.definitionFit: To go hungry is to go without food, the idiomatic sense of starve.

clue.text: Fainting once was funny with nothing on!

indicators.note: the word was is mixed up oddly

parts.note: O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: An archaic faint that seemed amusing when wearing nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: Aswoon is an archaic word for being in a swoon, a faint.

clue.text: See 25
Able to avoid the blame on completing tuition course for foreign students

indicators.note: the word on finishes off the course, coming after it

parts.note: TEFL is Teaching English as a Foreign Language

explanation.surface: Finishing a language course for overseas learners while dodging responsibility.
explanation.definitionFit: A Teflon politician is one to whom no blame or scandal sticks, from the non-stick coating.

clue.text: See 25
Religious figure seen breaking into extremely religious changing room

indicators.note: the saint is put inside the word for extremely

parts.note: extremely means very
ST, short for saint

explanation.surface: A saint invades a room where pious people get changed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'extremely religious' reads as one phrase, but 'religious' belongs to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A vestry is the room in a church where clergy put on their vestments.

clue.text: See 11
See 25
Hard to get into club, having 100 satang

indicators.note: the letter goes inside the club

parts.note: a bat is a club for hitting a ball
H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: Tough to gain entry to a club with one hundred coins.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition names the currency by what it holds: one baht is worth 100 satang.
explanation.definitionFit: The Thai baht is a currency unit divided into 100 satang.

clue.text: A look that's bad for environmentalist struggling for information when 17 south on …

indicators.note: these words are in difficulties, so their letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A green campaigner finds a disapproving look a problem.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition runs on into the next clue: an announcement when travelling south on the Northern line. 17 is TUBING, riding the London Underground.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the platform announcement giving the route of a southbound Northern line train.

clue.text: … line, or time the woman in the news

indicators.note: the pieces sit inside the pair of Ns

parts.note: N stands for new, so news, read as plural Ns, gives NN
her refers to a woman

explanation.surface: A remark about the time a woman spent in the headlines.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition joins on from the previous clue: the Northern line of the London Underground.
explanation.definitionFit: The Northern line is a London Underground line, so the adjective names the line.
